content:
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 70) and sentiment is weak, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0 point downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ true values if sentiment volatility > 0.30.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.10 to +0.17 over 3+ days, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2 points relative to prior 7-day average.
